items.title: Interpreting the Arrow Function Notation

sections.normalized_html:
Which of the following functions has the codomain [MATH: [0,1]?]

  1. [MATH: p: \{ 0, 1 \} \to \mathbb{R}]

  2. [MATH: q: \mathbb{R} \to [ 0, 1 ]]

  3. [MATH: r: [0,1] \to [ 0, 1 )]
sections.readable_text:
Which of the following functions has the codomain [MATH: [0,1]?]

1. [MATH: p: \{ 0, 1 \} \to \mathbb{R}]
2. [MATH: q: \mathbb{R} \to [ 0, 1 ]]
3. [MATH: r: [0,1] \to [ 0, 1 )]

sections.normalized_html: EXPLANATION
sections.readable_text: EXPLANATION

sections.normalized_html:
The notation [MATH: f: X \to Y] means that the function [MATH: f] maps the set [MATH: X] to the set [MATH: Y.] In this case,

  • the domain of [MATH: f] is [MATH: X,]

  • the codomain of [MATH: f] is [MATH: Y.]

With that in mind, let's examine our functions.

  • The codomain of [MATH: p] is [MATH: \mathbb{R},] the set of real numbers.

  • The codomain of [MATH: q] is [MATH: [ 0, 1 ],] the interval from [MATH: 0] and [MATH: 1] (including [MATH: 0] and [MATH: 1]).

  • The codomain of [MATH: r] is [MATH: [ 0, 1),] the interval from [MATH: 0] to [MATH: 1] (including [MATH: 0] but not including [MATH: 1]).

Therefore, the correct answer is "II only."

[MATH: \qquad] "The function [MATH: g] maps the set of rational numbers to the set [MATH: Y]."

  1. [MATH: g:\mathbb{Q} \to Y]

  2. [MATH: g: Y \to \mathbb{Q}]

  3. [MATH: g:\mathbb{R} \to Y]

2. [MATH: g: Y \to \mathbb{Q}]
3. [MATH: g:\mathbb{R} \to Y]

sections.readable_text: EXPLANATION

sections.normalized_html:
The sentence "The function [MATH: g] maps the set of rational numbers to the set [MATH: Y]" is equivalent to the following symbolic notation:

[MATH: \qquad] [MATH: g:\mathbb{Q} \to Y]

Here, the domain of [MATH: g] is [MATH: \mathbb Q,] and the codomain of [MATH: g] is [MATH: Y.]

Therefore, the correct answer is "I only".

Content:
A function relates an input to an output.
The set of all inputs is called the domain of the function, while the set of all possible outputs is the codomain of the function.

Content:
To say "the function [MATH: f] maps the set [MATH: X] to the set [MATH: Y,]" we can use the following notation:

Content:
[MATH: f : X \to Y]

Content:
In this case,

Content:
- the domain of [MATH: f] is [MATH: X,] and
- the codomain of [MATH: f] is [MATH: Y.]

Content:
You might be used to calling the set of outputs of a function as the range of the function. However, there is a subtle difference between codomain and range, which we'll learn about during this lesson.

---

Item 2 — Example: Interpreting the Arrow Function Notation

Example Prompt:
Which of the following functions has the codomain [MATH: [0,1]?]

1. [MATH: p: \{ 0, 1 \} \to \mathbb{R}]
2. [MATH: q: \mathbb{R} \to [ 0, 1 ]]
3. [MATH: r: [0,1] \to [ 0, 1 )]

Content:
EXPLANATION

Explanation:
The notation [MATH: f: X \to Y] means that the function [MATH: f] maps the set [MATH: X] to the set [MATH: Y.] In this case,

- the domain of [MATH: f] is [MATH: X,]
- the codomain of [MATH: f] is [MATH: Y.]

With that in mind, let's examine our functions.

- The codomain of [MATH: p] is [MATH: \mathbb{R},] the set of real numbers.
- The codomain of [MATH: q] is [MATH: [ 0, 1 ],] the interval from [MATH: 0] and [MATH: 1] (including [MATH: 0] and [MATH: 1]).
- The codomain of [MATH: r] is [MATH: [ 0, 1),] the interval from [MATH: 0] to [MATH: 1] (including [MATH: 0] but not including [MATH: 1]).

Therefore, the correct answer is "II only."

Item 5 — Example: Writing a Function Using Arrow Notation

Example Prompt:
Which of the following is the correct symbolic notation for the sentence given below?

[MATH: \qquad] "The function [MATH: g] maps the set of rational numbers to the set [MATH: Y]."

1. [MATH: g:\mathbb{Q} \to Y]
2. [MATH: g: Y \to \mathbb{Q}]
3. [MATH: g:\mathbb{R} \to Y]

Content:
EXPLANATION

Explanation:
The sentence "The function [MATH: g] maps the set of rational numbers to the set [MATH: Y]" is equivalent to the following symbolic notation:

[MATH: \qquad] [MATH: g:\mathbb{Q} \to Y]

Here, the domain of [MATH: g] is [MATH: \mathbb Q,] and the codomain of [MATH: g] is [MATH: Y.]

Therefore, the correct answer is "I only".

Item 8 — Tutorial: An Alternative Arrow Notation

Content:
The alternative arrow notation for a function "[MATH: \mapsto]" describes to which element of the codomain each element in the domain is mapped.

Content:
Consider the following function [MATH: f,] defined by the alternative arrow notation:

Content:
[MATH: f : x \mapsto |x|]

Content:
This means that the function [MATH: f] maps the element [MATH: x] in the domain to [MATH: |x|] in the codomain. Notice that this can also be written as

Content:
[MATH: f(x) = |x|.]

EXPLANATION

Therefore, the correct answer is "I only."

Item 12 — Tutorial: Codomain vs. Range

Content:
How do the codomain and range differ? Recall that in the notation [MATH: f : X \to Y] the codomain of the function is [MATH: Y.]

Content:
On the other hand, the range of [MATH: f] is the subset of the codomain that contains all values [MATH: y \in Y] that are mapped to by at least one element [MATH: x \in X.]

Content:
Consider the function [MATH: f(x)=|x|] shown in the mapping diagram below.

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/77623b027edde5d995e1f037d2d9faaa]

Content:
Inspecting the diagram, we see that:

Content:
- the domain of [MATH: f] is [MATH: X = \{ -2,-1,1,2,3 \},]
- the codomain of [MATH: f] is [MATH: Y = \{ 0,1,2,3,4 \},]
- the range of [MATH: f] is [MATH: \{ 1,2,3 \},] the subset of elements of [MATH: Y] that have at least one incoming arrow.

Content:
The range depends on the domain we choose. If we remove the element [MATH: 3] from the domain in the diagram above, then the element [MATH: 3] in the codomain will not have any incoming arrows. Therefore, the range of the function will be [MATH: \{ 1,2 \}.]

Item 13 — Example: Identifying Codomains and Ranges

Example Prompt:
Which of the following is the correct interpretation of [MATH: g: \{ -1,0,1 \} \to \mathbb{R}?]

1. The domain of [MATH: g] is [MATH: \{ -1,0,1 \}]
2. The codomain of [MATH: g] is [MATH: \mathbb{R}]
3. The range of [MATH: g] is [MATH: \mathbb{R}]

Content:
EXPLANATION

Explanation:
The notation

[MATH: g: \{ -1,0,1 \} \to \mathbb{R}]

means that the function [MATH: g] maps the set [MATH: \{ -1,0,1 \}] to the set [MATH: \mathbb{R}.] In this case,

- the domain of [MATH: g] is [MATH: \{ -1,0,1 \},] and
- the codomain of [MATH: g] is [MATH: \mathbb{R}.] Note that this is not necessarily the range.

As a result, statements I and II are true, while statement III is false.

Therefore, the correct answer is "I and II only."
